+# Incident Postmortem: High p99 Latency on booklogr-api
+
+## Root Cause
+The root cause of the high p99 HTTP latency (5.82s) was a regression introduced in commit `8c580a7` ("Scope search cache key to the authenticated user"). The `@cache.cached` decorator on the `/v1/books/search` endpoint was modified to include the authenticated user ID in the cache key (`key_prefix=lambda: f"view/{get_current_user_id()}/{request.path}"`). 
+
+Previously, the cache key was global. Because the external book search providers (`openlibrary.org` and the fallback API) are currently experiencing severe degradation or timeouts, the external API calls are extremely slow (taking 30-60s to time out). When the cache was global, these slow external requests were cached across all users, masking the external latency. However, after the regression, the cache became per-user. This change massively amplified the load on the slow external providers (scaling by $O(\text{users})$), causing Gunicorn worker threads to become completely saturated and queuing subsequent requests, resulting in the high p99 latency observed.
+
+## Evidence Used
+- Alerting stack flagged `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` with p99 latency at 5.82s.
+- Prometheus query `rate(flask_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="booklogr-api", path="/v1/books/search"}[1m])` confirmed the endpoint was receiving a sustained rate of ~3 requests per second.
+- `curl` tests from the container verified that both `openlibrary.org` and `metadata.booklogr.app` were taking 1+ minutes to return/timeout.
+- Reviewing `api/routes/books.py` and git history showed the cache scoping change.
+
+## What Was Changed
+- The `@cache.cached` decorator was completely removed from the `search_books` route, as caching the local DB search per user alongside the external data is unnecessary.
+- Manual caching was introduced around the `BookProvider().search(search_term)` call inside `search_books`. This explicitly restores the global cache for the slow external API calls using the key `f"ext_search_{search_term}"`.
+- This change ensures that external provider lookups remain globally cached to minimize latency, while local user data remains scoped to the authenticated user without being leaked across the cache.
